display.purpose: DICEMORE hero title only — one element per session, rise-entrance animated.

header.purpose: Step titles, modal titles, class card names — the primary decision-making tier.

title.purpose: Enemy names, sub-section labels, content titles inside cards.

body.purpose: Descriptions, subtitles, tutorial copy. Wordwrapped inside cards.

label.purpose: Rarity badges, status pills, intent hint text, small numerical indicators.

motion.name: scene-fade-out
motion.purpose: Every scene exit before scene.start(). 180ms HomeScene, 200ms SetupScene/BattleScene.

motion.name: title-entrance
motion.purpose: DICEMORE title rises into frame on HomeScene create.

motion.name: button-stagger
motion.purpose: HomeScene button/descriptor stagger after title settles.

motion.name: danger-pulse
motion.value: tween alpha→0.10, duration 700, Sine.InOut, yoyo, repeat -1
motion.purpose: Critical HP indicator — triggers at ≤25% playerMaxHp.

motion.name: intent-pop
motion.purpose: Enemy bumper pop when intent changes — draws eye to new threat.

motion.name: bumper-flash
motion.purpose: Bumper contact feedback — both enemy and player bumpers.

motion.name: commit-entrance
motion.purpose: Commit overlay rises into view after all dice thrown.

motion.name: bumper-glow
motion.purpose: Enemy bumper outer glow ring — ambient, marks physics body.

breakpoints.name: canvas
breakpoints.purpose: Portrait-only fixed canvas. No responsive breakpoints within the game.

components.name: Primary Button (Gold)
components.description: Main action button — SOLO, DICE DUEL. Rectangular, gold stroke, dark fill floods subtly on hover.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: #131320; color: #f0c040; font-family: "Cinzel", serif; font-size: 22px; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 3px; padding: 14px 24px; border: 2px solid rgba(240, 192, 64, 0.9); border-radius: 0; cursor: pointer; width: 240px; transition: background 0.12s; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #1e2840; } .ds-btn-primary:active { background: #273050; }

components.name: Confirm Button (Green)
components.description: Commit-to-action button — Begin Battle, End Turn, Next. Fill floods green on hover — aggressive confirmation signal.
components.css: .ds-btn-confirm { background: #163824; color: #aaffaa; font-family: system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 17px; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 2px; padding: 14px 24px; border: 1.5px solid rgba(39, 174, 96, 0.9); border-radius: 0; cursor: pointer; width: 100%; max-width: 360px; transition: background 0.12s, color 0.12s; } .ds-btn-confirm:hover { background: #27ae60; color: #ffffff; }

components.name: Destructive Button (Quit)
components.description: Used inside quit confirm dialog. No hover treatment — certainty required.
components.css: .ds-btn-destructive { font-family: "Cinzel", serif; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 700; color: #ee6644; background: #1a0a08; border: none; padding: 7px 16px; cursor: pointer; } .ds-btn-destructive:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #ee6644; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Class Card (Dice Slinger)

narrative.overview:
Dicemore is set in an underground western gambling championship where The Devil runs the event and everyone cheats. The UI is the Parlor's interior: near-black surfaces tinted toward deep navy, gold serif lettering that declares the stakes, and a physics surface where dice do not care about your plans.

This is not a bright mobile game. It is not a generic dark UI. It is a specific kind of dark: the dark of a room where serious things happen under low, deliberate light. Every pixel of contrast is earned. Every animation has a job. Numbers feel heavy because the game is playing for keeps.

The references PRODUCT.md names — Balatro and Slay the Spire — share one property: their UI cannot be moved to another game. Dicemore's gold Cinzel headers, die-shape visual language, and tonal depth stack must earn the same recognition.
keyCharacteristics: Dark-first backgrounds (near-black with blue hue lean) at every layer
Cinzel for display type; system sans for body — contrast axis, not similarity axis
Stroke-not-fill interactions: dark fill with colored stroke; fill floods on hover
Mechanical color: die types own their colors permanently — never decorative use
Flat geometry; circles only for functional physics bodies (bumpers, relic indicators)
Camera fades on all scene transitions; within-scene steps crossfade at 160/220ms
Header strip (y=0–80) reserved permanently for phase/status/navigation

rules.name: The Closed Mechanic Rule
rules.body: The five die mechanic colors are permanent and exclusive. They appear on die symbols, class card shapes, and status pills — nowhere else. Break this rule and the visual language stops working.

rules.name: The One Gold Rule
rules.body: Parlor Gold (#f0c040) touches ≤3 elements per screen. Its power comes from its rarity. Do not apply it to interactive elements that need to communicate anything other than Dicemore's identity.

rules.name: The Danger Signal Rule
rules.body: #ff1100 is used exclusively as the critical-HP danger pulse overlay (alpha ≤ 0.10, 700ms yoyo). Its association with mortal danger must not be diluted by any decorative use.

rules.name: The Three Spacings Rule
rules.body: letterSpacing has exactly three valid values: 0 (body), 3 (Cinzel headers/buttons), 6 (hero title only). No other values.

rules.name: The Cinzel Ceiling Rule
rules.body: Cinzel is prohibited below 14px. The letterforms collapse at small sizes. Any text below 14px uses system-ui only.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces at rest cast no shadows. Hover states use fill-color lightening, not shadow elevation. Add drop shadows and the game starts looking like a web app.

rules.name: The Dim-Not-Blur Rule
rules.body: Modals occlude via 0x000000 at 0.65–0.70 alpha. No blur, no backdrop-filter. The performance budget belongs to Matter.js physics simulation.

dos: Do use Cinzel only for display text ≥14px. Below that size, always system-ui.
Do keep Parlor Gold (#f0c040) to ≤3 elements per screen. Its rarity is its power.
Do use camera fades (180–350ms black) on every scene transition. Instant cuts read as prototype.
Do reserve die mechanic colors exclusively for mechanical contexts — die symbols, class card shapes, status pills, intent text. Never decorative.
Do express depth through fill darkness only: #080f1c → #0d0d1c → #13192e → #111122. No drop shadows.
Do use the dim overlay (0x000000 at 0.65 alpha) when a modal or picker opens.
Do verify HP numbers, die values, and damage text hit ≥4.5:1 contrast on their background.
Do accompany every color-coded indicator with a type label (ATK/BLK/STR). Color is never the sole differentiator.
Do use the danger pulse (#ff1100, alpha ≤ 0.10, 700ms Sine.InOut yoyo) exclusively for critical HP. One signal, one meaning.
Do extend the die-shape convention (triangle/square/diamond) to any new die type added.
donts: Don't use soft pastels, rounded bubbly elements, or 'safe stakes' energy. Per PRODUCT.md: this game has teeth.
Don't add coin-pop animations, bright primary colors, or in-your-face progression noise. Dicemore is not a generic free-to-play mobile game.
Don't ship a UI element that could belong to a different game without feeling wrong.
Don't use #ff1100 (danger red) for anything except the critical-HP overlay.
Don't add drop shadows to surfaces. The depth system is tonal only.
Don't use letterSpacing values outside 0, 3, or 6 for Cinzel text.
Don't add border-radius greater than 4px to buttons or cards. 12px radius belongs in a different game.
Don't put decorative animation on informational state changes. The danger pulse means danger; repurposing it destroys the signal.
Don't add a new die type without assigning it a dedicated color that appears across all surfaces.
Don't render die types as text labels (BUF d4, CPY d4) on class cards — the geometric shape language exists to replace those labels.
